html:
The largest city of India and its money capital, on the west coast. It was built on seven islands that were joined by land reclamation, and was called Bombay until 1995.

The islands were home to Koli fishing people. The Sultanate of Gujarat gave them to Portugal in 1534. In 1661 they passed to England as part of the dowry of Catherine of Braganza, and in 1668 the Crown leased them to the East India Company. Its deep harbour slowly drew trade from Surat, and Parsi, Gujarati, Konkani and other merchants settled there.

In the 1800s Bombay boomed. India's first passenger train ran from it in 1853. During the American Civil War, cotton prices soared and the city's traders grew rich, and cotton mills followed. The Bombay Stock Exchange dates from 1875, the year the Arya Samaj was founded there. Plague struck in 1896. Families such as the founders of the Tata Group built industry, and the Reserve Bank of India moved its head office to the city in 1937. The dabbawalas still carry home-cooked lunches to its office workers.

The Indian National Congress first met in Bombay in 1885. After independence the city was the centre of the Progressive Artists' Group and of Hindi cinema, known as Bollywood.
sum: The largest city of India and its money capital, on the west coast. It was built on seven islands that were joined by land reclamation, and was called Bombay until 1995.
